data.narrative:
Tokamak Energy, a Series C nuclear energy company that has raised $335M+, sits within a fragmented frontier-tech sector. The nuclear energy comp universe spans 10 companies (3 public, 7 private), including peers such as Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, and Fuse Energy. However, the narrow peer set presents a significant analytical constraint.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised as a valuation proxy ($335M), a typical Series C-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.7x implies a valuation of $570M. A peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient comparable data points at the same stage or adjacent stages within the nuclear energy sector; this constraint reflects the nascency and heterogeneity of the frontier-tech nuclear market rather than a data collection failure.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $484M (low) to $655M (median ±$85M), anchored to a $570M median. This range reflects both stage-typical expansion and a meaningful uncertainty band appropriate to a single-method derivation. Key sensitivities include the applicability of the 1.7x multiplier to this specific subsector and the absence of public market comparables at similar capital levels or development milestones. Further valuation confidence would require either additional same-stage private financings or a broadening into adjacent clean-energy sectors.
